sentence: This project studies how epsilon toxin from Clostridium perfringens, linked to Multiple Sclerosis, causes disease and gets past immune privilege, using mutant mice.
This project studies how changes in many genes work together to cause spina bifida, using DNA sequencing and computation methods.
This project builds a platform that finds mimics of the targets of T cells, to help treat autoimmunity and transplant rejection.
This project brings scientists together to discuss how skeletal muscle stem cells control muscle growth, repair, aging and disease.
This project builds tools, including artificial intelligence and robotics, that help scientists collect and analyze X-ray data on crystals of proteins.
This project builds a center that manages, standardizes and shares brain and behavior data, and offers a cloud-based platform to analyze it.
This project studies how hearing loss, hearing aids and cochlear implants change how information from both ears is processed.
This project develops an imaging technique and a treatment plan that aim to protect normal liver function during radiation for liver tumors.
This project gives cancer researchers biostatistics and clinical research informatics support, including machine learning to find risk factors.
This project uses a mouse model and mass spectrometry imaging to study the short- and long-term molecular effects of acute organophosphate poisoning.
This project engineers a self-activating receptor to help T cells suppress autoimmune disease or increase the antitumor immune response.
This project studies how low levels of a serine biosynthesis pathway protein raise sialic acid production and promote metastasis of triple negative breast cancer.
This project tries to find out why chronically active pulmonary sarcoidosis is linked to peripheral lymphopenia and T-cell dysfunction.
This project brings researchers together to discuss how experience changes gene regulation in the brain and how disruption of it causes disorders.
This project tries to improve an imaging and therapeutic approach that shows whether breast tumors respond to or resist trastuzumab-drug conjugates.
This project studies the sequence, structure and variation of human centromeres and how they ensure equal segregation of chromosomes.
This project builds a functional genomics platform that uses CRISPR screening in human neurons to find molecules that organize synapse formation.
This project designs and tests variants of a viral protein that inhibits inflammation and binds chemokines, to map how they interact.
This project provides data analysis support for osteoarthritis studies, including reviewing analysis plans and using machine learning.
This project tests whether an oral Janus kinase inhibitor safely stops autoimmune destruction of insulin-producing beta-cells in checkpoint inhibitor-induced diabetes.
